classificationNotes: Source-draft Lizardfolk are treated as a reptilian visual and encounter-production family, not as an accepted biological people or a universal statement about culture, technology, intelligence, social rank, personhood, habitat, or hostility. Source swamp and tribal imagery becomes explicit equipment and arena grammar rather than essentialized identity.
visualConstants: An upright forward-leaning reptilian body keeps clawed hands and feet, a long counterbalancing tail, a crocodilian or iguana-like head, and an escalating dorsal ridge.
Swamp green, mud brown, moss, and ocher are punctuated by warning-bright orange, red, or yellow throat and crest colors.
Scale, bone, obsidian, hide, river reed, ordinary mud, and feather remain separately legible materials.
Paint, bone piercings, trophy skulls, woven shields, and feather headdresses accumulate without obscuring natural plating.
Tail angle, crest posture, dorsal plates, hands, and planted feet preserve the direction and recovery of each attack.
escalationAxis: Crest height, dorsal spines, natural plating, tail weaponization, and control of marked hunting ground grow from a lean scout to a sovereign back-sail war court.

constructionDimensions: Family-native, non-affinity swamp habitat, ordinary mud, damp scales, moss colors, river reed, obsidian, and environmental wetness remain physical context rather than Water or Earth affinity construction.
Movement stays bodily and equipment-driven: tails balance, claws dig into soil, shields flex, mud flakes or splashes under weight, and warning colors remain pigment without supernatural wake.
normal.counterplaySignal: The loaded tail base, planted foot, shield weave, dorsal gap, or mantle tie preserves each form's established weak point.
forbidden: unexplained elemental anatomy
unexplained elemental glow
unexplained environmental wake
Treating swamp water, mud, wet scales, moss color, or ordinary splashes as affinity evidence

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe construction: T1 Scout uses ember-cut bone spear points, charred hide wrap, a pitch cord along the tail, and fired-clay guards on existing scale rows and planted feet; T2 Warrior may vent through its low crest and reed shield; T3–T5 may mount heat-resistant bone vents only around their mature dorsal spines and armor.
Actions show fuel and cooling through T1 spear-wick smoke and a matte tail scale, T2 shield-edge ignition, and T3–T5 directional smoke along the selected dorsal gap and obsidian weapon.
fire.counterplaySignal: T1 Scout exposes the pitch cord between its bone spear, hide wrap, and tail before ignition; T2 Warrior exposes the low-crest vent or shield wrap, while T3–T5 expose the matte dorsal gap during cooldown.
forbidden: Palette-only orange or red scales that duplicate family warning colors
Glow-only fire treatment without fuel, combustion, and cooling structure
Flame anatomy replacing crest, dorsal plates, tail, or obsidian gear
Smoke that conceals planted feet or tail direction

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe construction: T1 Scout uses a mineral-capped bone spear, grit-stiffened hide wrap, fitted guards on existing scale rows, a tail counterweight, and wedges beneath planted feet; T2 Warrior may laminate its shield and low crest; T3–T5 may place crystal wedges between mature dorsal plates and heavier natural armor.
Locomotion becomes load-bearing through the T1 planted foot and fractured spear cap, the T2 shield anchor, and T3–T5 compressed strata at the active dorsal wedge or tail weight.
earth.counterplaySignal: T1 Scout locks one planted foot into a mineral ring while the bone spear cap turns chalk-white; T2 Warrior exposes its low-crest or shield anchor, while T3–T5 expose the loaded dorsal wedge before release.
forbidden: Palette-only brown scales or extra mud without fitted mineral structure
Glow-only earth treatment without anchors, weight, and fractures
Ordinary swamp mud presented alone as Earth affinity
Stone bulk that erases the agile reptilian silhouette

constructionDimensions: Tier-safe construction: T1 Scout uses whistle holes in the bone spear, a vented hide wrap, tail streamers, and vane strips tied to existing scale rows and planted feet; T2 Warrior may add reed panels and vanes to its low crest; T3–T5 may add hollow flutes and pressure vanes only along mature dorsal spines and mantles.
Motion exposes pressure through the T1 spear whistle and tail line, the T2 shield flex, and T3–T5 coherent streamlines that leave a still pocket behind the loaded dorsal ridge.
wind.counterplaySignal: T1 Scout aligns its bone spear, hide-wrap vane, and tail streamer down one lane while a planted foot stays still; T2 Warrior aligns low-crest vanes and reed slats, while T3–T5 expose the silent dorsal gap from the lee.
forbidden: Palette-only pale scales without flutes, vanes, and directional pressure
Glow-only wind treatment without a force route and still center
Ordinary feathers or tail balancing presented alone as Wind affinity
Floating or turbulence that hides planted reptilian footwork

constructionDimensions: Affinity construction adds shell valves, reed reservoirs, translucent pressure bladders, channel-cut obsidian, and capillary hide bands beyond ordinary swamp dampness.
Actions show coherent fill and drainage through darkening scale rows, measured jets along spear, shield, blade, or tail, wet reflections, and an exposed valve after pressure loss.
water.counterplaySignal: A reed bladder swells and one scale row darkens before a pressure action; puncture it or open the exposed shell valve after release.
forbidden: Palette-only blue-green scales or ordinary swamp wetness without hydraulic construction
Glow-only water treatment without reservoirs, coherent flow, and drainage
Shapeless liquid anatomy replacing natural scales or equipment
Opaque spray that hides claws, tail, crest, or counterplay valve

forms.battlefieldDuty: Probe lateral spacing with one bone-spear feint whose true thrust follows the counterbalancing tail.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that the tail reveals attack direction before the spear and leaves the no-crest initiate exposed if displaced.
forms.signatureMechanic: Countertail Jab: the Scout swings its long tail opposite the upcoming spear thrust, committing both body axes.
forms.telegraph: Ordinary mud flakes from the lean body, the simple hide wrap twists, and the long tail sweeps away from the bone spear.
forms.counterplay: Step toward the moving tail rather than the spear and strike the planted rear foot during the fixed jab.
forms.visualDelta: Small, lean, mud-caked, and explicitly crestless with a bone spear and simple hide wrap.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Hold a repeatable close line with a woven shield while an obsidian-toothed club attacks around one side.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to read shield weave tension and cross the unpainted side before the club follows.
forms.signatureMechanic: Reed Lock: the Warrior bows its woven shield into an angled brace, then swings the toothed club only along the war-painted snout side.
forms.telegraph: Reed fibers pull taut, the low forming crest rises, and snout paint aligns with the club shoulder.
forms.counterplay: Cross the unpainted shield edge or cut its taut reed binding, exposing the torso before the club can reverse.
forms.visualDelta: A low crest, obsidian-toothed club, woven reed shield, and war paint mature the baseline reptilian soldier.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Scouts jab past the braced shield, but cutting its weave also exposes their predictable countertail lane.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Qualitatively pivot the encounter by turning heavy dorsal spines into a one-way mobile gate that partitions the battlefield while twin blades threaten its open hinge.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach that natural plating now edits space: follow which spine row lowers and attack through that temporary gate.
forms.signatureMechanic: Spine Gate: the Spineback crouches and fans alternate dorsal spines into a barrier, leaving one visibly lowered segment as a passage; twin obsidian blades cover only the alligator-jaw side of that passage.
forms.telegraph: Heavy dorsal spines rise in sequence, chest plate-scales lock, the alligator jaw opens toward one side, and one spine segment remains flat.
forms.counterplay: Pass through the flat segment from the side opposite the jaw, strike its exposed root, or force the Specialist to turn and collapse the gate.
forms.visualDelta: Heavy dorsal spines, thick chest plate-scales, alligator jaw, and twin obsidian blades create a spatial-control silhouette rather than a larger Warrior.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Warriors brace the closed spine segments and Scouts stab through gaps; breaking the lowered root folds the barrier and removes their protected lanes.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Command a rotating hunting ring, using a tail-club and trophy skulls to assign lower forms to the open segment.
forms.teachingGoal: Teach players to read headdress and tail commitment, then break the trophy tied to the active formation.
forms.signatureMechanic: Four Hunts: four trophy skulls hang from crocodilian shoulder plating. The Chieftain strikes one with its tail-club to assign Scout jabs, Warrior shields, or Spineback gates to a quarter-ring, then sweeps only that marked quarter.
forms.telegraph: The feather headdress tilts, one skull rattles, and the heavy tail-club draws a groove toward the selected quarter.
forms.counterplay: Leave the marked quarter, cut its hanging skull during the tail recovery, and use the resulting gap in the lower-form ring.
forms.visualDelta: Crocodilian bulk, trophy skulls on shoulder plating, feathered headdress, and a mature tail-club form the champion silhouette.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Each trophy calls Scouts, Warriors, or a Spineback into a familiar duty; destroying it removes that quarter's formation until the encounter ends.

forms.battlefieldDuty: Transform a five-mark hunting ground through a full back-sail crest, ordering lower forms until each cut mantle tie lowers one sail section and removes a phase rule.
forms.teachingGoal: Test tail direction, shield weave, spine gates, and trophy quarters while permanent sail collapse turns a formation boss into a readable grounded duel.
forms.signatureMechanic: Five Marks of the Sail: five painted panels on the full back-sail map to arena markings. Bone calls Scouts across one line, Reed braces Warriors, Obsidian raises a Spineback gate, Skull orders a Chieftain quarter, and Stone commits the Tyrant's own tail-club through the surviving marks. The ceremonial feather-and-hide mantle is tied once beneath each panel. After the selected learned pattern resolves, its tie stretches across the dorsal gap; cutting it folds that sail panel, erases the mark, and removes the command. With two panels left, the mantle falls and the Tyrant must plant before every tail sweep.
forms.telegraph: One body-painted sail panel rises, the matching mantle tie pulls taut, its arena mark is exposed, and the chosen lower form assumes its known posture.
forms.counterplay: Use the selected lower-form response, reach the exposed dorsal tie, and cut it; every collapsed panel permanently removes one command and opens that section of the arena.
forms.visualDelta: A full back-sail crest, ceremonial feather-and-hide mantle, stone tail-club, and war paint across the entire plated body create an unmistakable sovereign mechanism.
forms.lowerFormInteraction: Scout, Warrior, Spineback, and Swamp Chieftain each occupy a painted sail mark; cutting that panel's tie ends the linked lower-form pattern for all later phases.
